He based on this recognition his saying, indicating by the passive form the ease of seizing them by any seizer whatsoever: ﴿So they will be seized by the forelocks﴾, that is, from them, and these are the forepart of the heads, ﴿and the feet﴾, after the two are gathered together, just as they used to join what God commanded to be separated, and separate what God commanded to be joined. Thus they will be dragged with them, dragged by every dragger whom God has appointed for that purpose, unable to resist in any way, and so they will be cast into the Fire.

When that was a blessing whose thanks cannot be rendered by everyone who hears of it, because every person would wish to be free from criminality and would love for the criminals the greatest retribution, He made the following a consequence of it, saying: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ That is: of the great blessings from the One who arranged your interests after bringing you into existence. ﴿Will you both deny?﴾ Is it the blessing of being seized by the forelock from behind, or other than it, of what must be done as recompense in the Hereafter for each person according to what he used to do in this world, or other than that of bounty?

When their being seized in this manner indicated that they would end up in great disgrace, he made it explicit in His words, building on what the context pointed to, namely: a seizing spoken of when they reach the place of punishment, in the state mentioned of being seized by their forelocks and feet,

﴿This is﴾ [i.e., the] great pit, hideous in appearance, ["near to you"] [close to you, continually near at hand] ﴿Hell, which the guilty deny﴾. That is, denying it in the past, present, and future, out of contempt. Even if they were returned to the world after being made to enter it, ﴿they would go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28] ﴿by it, the criminals﴾, i.e., those who are deeply immersed in crime, which is cutting off what ought to be joined, [and it is] what God commanded to be joined. He singled out this name to indicate that it will meet them with scowling, frowning, sullenness and harshness, just as they used to treat the righteous when committing the crime [mentioned]. Ibn Burjan said: ʿAbd Allah recited, "This is Hell, which you used to deny. You will burn in it; you will neither die therein nor live."

Then he resumed (mentioning) what will be done to them therein, saying: ﴿They will circulate between it﴾, i.e., between the abode of the Fire that scowls at them, ﴿and between boiling water﴾, i.e., water that is hot, so intensely hot that it has smoke (rising from it).

Since this term (ʾānin, "boiling") is also applied to cold water, he clarified its meaning, saying: ﴿boiling﴾, i.e., whose heat has reached an extreme beyond which there is no further extreme. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': It has also been said: "present" (ḥāḍir). It is from this that the present time is called al-ān ("the now"), because it is the present and existing moment, for the past cannot be recovered and the future is a hope, and we have nothing but the now. Then "the now" does not remain fixed even for the twinkling of an eye, for al-ān is the common part between two times. Thus they are constantly moving back and forth between the two torments: the Fire that melts the outside, and the water that cuts up the inside with its heat. It (the torment) never ceases to be present for them, a continual circulating without beginning to its circulation nor end.

The punishment of the criminal, which cuts off what would otherwise be continuous, is among the greatest and most delightful of blessings for everyone, even for other criminals. This led to His saying ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ That is, to You, O two weighty ones (al-Thaqalan, i.e., jinn and humankind), the Benefactor to you both by destroying the criminal in both abodes and by saving the believer from what He destroyed the criminal with, as a kindness to those who are warned, so that they may refrain and desist from what would cause their own destruction and that of those who follow them. ﴿Will you both deny?﴾ The blessing of the fire on the right, or other of His signs that He has shown you, and the clear proofs He has manifested to you, in the heavens and the earth, and what He has shown you of the rising-places of the world, such as the sun, which is the sign of the day, and the moon, which is the sign of the zamharir (the intense cold of the night), and other of His firm, visible and audible signs. This verse was repeated seven times after the mention of the Fire and its terrors, as a reminder of how to ward off its seven gates, as has passed. And God is the One sought for help.

When he had described the lot of the sinful one who dares to commit grave offenses, and placed it first because the context of wrathful warning required that, and made it seven, pointing to the seven gates of Hell, he followed it with the lot of the one who fears, whose fear led him to obedience, and made it [eight], corresponding to [the number of] the eight gates of Paradise. He said: ﴿And for whoever﴾ [i.e.,] and for each [person who]. He made the pronoun singular, observing the wording of "whoever" (man), pointing to the fewness of those who fear, ﴿fears﴾, that is, of the two weights (humans and jinn).

Since mention of fear of the time appointed for the reckoning [and the arrangement, and the place prepared for them both] is more eloquent than mention of fear of the King who reckons [and arranges], and since fear accompanied by mention of the attribute of honor is more eloquent than fear mentioned alongside the attributes of majesty, he said, indicating thereby that the one mentioned is the head of those who fear: ﴿the station of his Lord﴾, that is: the place of his standing, which he sets up, and in which he makes others stand, the Benefactor, for judgment, and the time that He appointed for him, and His standing over him and over [others] in managing affairs. So He is watchful over him and over them. How much more so when one recalls the station of the Avenger, the Compeller, the Proud. Thus he abandons for this what displeases Him and does what pleases Him. ﴿Two gardens﴾, on the right and on the left: one for knowledge and intellect, and the other for action. The dual may also be taken to express emphasis, conveying that they are gardens repeated and multiplied, like His words: ﴿Cast into Hell every stubborn disbeliever﴾ [Qaf: 24], and the like.

Since this was a comprehensive blessing, he made it the basis for His saying: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ That is: what an excellent Cherisher He is to you both, and what a benefactor to you with His great kindnesses, of which no one else is able to grant any part. ﴿Will you deny?﴾ Is it the blessing of the cool breeze from the shade (al-yasar) that arises from the heart, or other things from the soil of the gardens of this world, by the breath of Jahannam, from the heat of the sun and its scorching? So He made from that all the fruits and crops, and other necessities which He cooked with it. ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ [Yusuf: 105], and other of His countless blessings.

Since gardens cannot have their praise made complete except through the abundance of kinds and colors, and of intertwined branches and boughs, He said, describing the two: ﴿Thawata﴾, meaning possessors of, with the root letter restored, since its original form is "dhawu" ﴿of branches﴾, meaning plural of fann (kind), in which fruits are of varied sorts, and fanan, which is the branch that stands straight in length, by which there is adornment with leaves and fruit and complete benefit. ʿAtaʾ said: on every branch there are varieties of fruit. For this reason, He made the following statement a consequence of it:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 49:

﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [That is]: the One who nurtures you both and bestows goodness upon you both. ﴿Would you deny﴾ the blessing of the Shamm, from the direction of above or otherwise, of what He has mentioned to you of the description of the Garden, which He made for you, from its likenesses, [things] by which you may take warning?

Since gardens cannot stand without rivers, He said: ﴿In both of them are two springs﴾, meaning in each one there is a spring, ﴿flowing﴾, meaning in whatever place its owner wishes, even if the place is high, just as water rises in trees into every branch of them. And if their height increases, it flows over the two eyes of his tears that flow out of fear of Allah. This is on the pattern of the gardens of this world, when the sun is rising in the northern constellations (al-buruj al-shamaliyya), from the fullness of waters and their gushing forth as springs in the days of spring and summer, due to the nearness of the time since the rains.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 51:

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ That is, the Owner of you both and the One who bestows His kindness upon you both. ﴿Will you deny…﴾ the blessing of the two springs flowing from below [or other than that], of what He has mentioned, and which He has made in the world as many similitudes.

Since water is the source of plants' life and growth, He said, mentioning the best of plants: ﴿in both of them﴾, that is, these two lofty gardens. And by His saying ﴿of every fruit﴾, that is, which you know or do not know, ﴿two kinds﴾ (p-182), that is, two types, one of which completes the other, He indicated all that is known and more, just as the reality of either of the two pairs is not grasped except through acting in what pleases [God], and the other through refraining from what displeases [Him].

﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord will you deny?﴾ That is: the great favors which the Originator, the Benefactor to you both, nurtured for you. ﴿Will you deny?﴾ Is it the blessing of touch from the front, or other than it, that He originated for you the gardens of this world through the medium of the heat of the Fire, which is the greatest of your enemies? This is an indication that He is able, by His good pleasure and His love, to bring forth from the place of His wrath and His vengeance, as an honor. For He has made what is in this world an example of what He mentioned concerning the Hereafter. So with which of these things will you deny? Faith is not complete until the believer affirms that He, exalted is He, is able to make of Hell a Paradise, by making from the place of His displeasure a mercy, and that He wills this, and that he take heed of this through what He has shown us of its model.

Since enjoying fruit is not complete in its pleasure without luxury, such as fine cushions and other comforts, he said, informing about those who fear the standing before their Lord from among humankind and the jinn, observing the meaning of "min" after observing its wording, to affirm the reality: ﴿reclining﴾. That is, they have what was mentioned while reclining. This is establishing oneself in the posture of one sitting cross-legged or in another position, namely lying on one side. In al-Qamus (the dictionary of al-Fayruzabadi): "tawakka'a 'alayhi" means he relied on it, leaned on it, and depended on it, like "awka'a." The "tuka'ah," with a fatha or kasra on the first letter and a hamza, is a staff, or whatever one leans on. "Darabahu fa-atka'ahu" means he struck him and made him fall into the posture of one reclining, or onto his left side. Ibn al-Qatta' said: "Wa-darabtuhu hatta atka'tuhu" (I struck him until I made him recline), that is, he fell onto his side. This indicates the completeness of luxury through physical health and freedom from worry. ﴿On furnishings﴾, and he magnified them by his saying, addressing the responsible ones according to what their minds can bear, since there is nothing in Paradise that truly resembles them, nothing of this world. ﴿Their linings﴾, that is, how much more then their outer surfaces and faces, ﴿are of istabraq﴾, which is thick dibaj (brocade silk). Due to its beauty there is a sheen in it, as if [from] the intensity of its gleam it seeks to bring itself into being, until it is as if it were pure light.

Since the one reclining may find it burdensome to stand to take what he wants, he said: ﴿And the clusters of the two gardens﴾, that is, what is picked from them, a noun in the sense of the object, as if he expressed it this way to convey the ease of the very act of picking, which is the gathering. ﴿Near﴾, that is, close to everyone who wants it, whether reclining or otherwise, who does not need to go out to climb a tree, and it is available at all times whenever desired, not cut off nor forbidden.

Since it may be that a similar example is witnessed in this, [in the form of] branches that bend down entirely so that they come near, and others that are close to the trunk of the tree so that picking from them is easy, He said: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ That is: the great, kingly blessings which this Cherisher of yours, who is able to do whatever He wills, brought into being for you both. ﴿Will you deny⁠﻿ the blessing of touch from behind, or any other of His power over bending the branches and bringing the fruits near?﴾

(p-184) Since the blessing described cannot be complete except with beautiful women, He said, indicating multiplicity after the context of favour, using the plural, which is more fitting than the dual, to show that in every garden there is a company of women, because of the great pleasure and excessive intimacy they provide: ﴿Therein﴾, i.e., in the gardens, of which it has been known from what preceded that each one of those who fear [their Lord] has two gardens. And since the context of favour defines that the plural of paucity (jam' al-qilla) is intended to mean multiplicity, along with what has been mentioned of its embellishments in Surah Sad, He said, expressing it: ﴿Restraining their glances﴾, i.e., women kept in seclusion, who are obligated to veil so that they are not mentioned except by description without explicit naming; they have restrained their glances and their aspirations to their husbands, and they possess such beauty by which they restrain their husbands from turning toward others, because of the languor of the glance, its enchantment, and its strong capture of hearts, as a recompense to them for restricting their aspirations in this world to their Lord.

And since exclusivity with a thing, especially a woman, is among the greatest of pleasures, [He said:] ﴿Untouched﴾, i.e., not having lain with them, nor having exercised authority over them in this creation in which they were brought into being, any kind of authority, whether from humans or jinn or otherwise. It is said: "tamathat al-mar'ah" (like daraba and fariha): she menstruated; and "tamathaha al-rajul": he deflowered her, and also had intercourse with her; and "tamatha al-ba'ir": you tied the camel's knee. So it is as if it were said: they are virgins, the place of deflowering in them not having been touched ﴿by any human﴾. And since the intended meaning is generalizing the time, he dropped the preposition and said: ﴿before them﴾, i.e., before the reclining ones, ﴿nor jinn﴾. This covers every being with whom intercourse is possible, both outwardly and inwardly, and in it is evidence that a jinn may cover a human, as has been reported from al-Zajjaj.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 57:

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ That is: the great blessings from the Nurturer, the Perfect in knowledge, the All-encompassing in power, the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyum). ﴿Will you deny?﴾ Is it the blessing of touch, from the right side or from other than it, or what Allah has made for you as a likeness of this among the virgin maidens of beauty, or other kinds of kindness?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 58:

When what preceded of the description of those who are enjoyed by them (the maidens) in terms of preciousness and excellence had indicated this, he added to it in a manner that conveys that through them there would be the utmost of tranquility of soul, strength of heart, vigor of body, balance of blood, and other special qualities of that to which he likened them. So He said: ﴿As if they were rubies﴾, which, in its clarity, is such that its thread shows through it, and it is a known gem. In al-Qamus he said: "The finest of it is the red, pomegranate-colored kind; it is beneficial for whisperings (waswas), palpitation, and weakness of the heart when drunk, and for thickening of the blood when hung (as an amulet)." ﴿And coral﴾ in its whiteness; and small pearls are purer in whiteness. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz said: "Marjan is small pearls, and this which comes out of the plants of the sea is a known red" — end of quote. It may be derived from this that their colors are whiteness and redness with a kind of tinge which is most admirable in terms of transparency and clarity, and which, together with that, is constant and does not undergo change, in conformity with the hadith in which it says: "The marrow of her shin can be seen from behind seventy garments." And Abu Hayyan said: He likened them to these two in respects in which likening is fitting: the ruby in its smoothness and transparency, and the coral in its smoothness and the beauty of its appearance.

[p. 186] ﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ That is, which of the extraordinary blessings, surpassing in beauty, from the Owner, the King, the One who nurtures with wondrous nurture? ﴿Will you both deny﴾: is it the blessing of touch from the direction of the left, or other blessings like it? He made this an example of what He mentioned about their description, namely comparing one thing to two things, because the matter reaches such a degree of beauty that no single thing can equal it, so that it may be compared to it. Thus, as it has been said:

White in the intensity of the black of the eye,
yellow in the na'aj,
as if she were silver, to which gold has been mixed.

Glorified is He, He has made transparent things a likeness for this. You see some bodies through which the face can almost be seen. [Indeed, in the blackness of the eye is the greatest brightness, for through it the face can be seen.] For blackness is the origin of darkness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 60:

When the most delightful of the blessings a person obtains is that which was caused by his own effort, He said, gladdening them by this, together with the delight of praise, especially since the One praising is the Supreme King, extolling them by way of a rhetorical question, which affirms after a negation that conveys exclusivity, in the manner of strong disapproval toward those who imagine otherwise: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ That is: in the deed [that occurs] from humans or jinn or others ﴿anything but good﴾, that is, in the reward. This is among the places where the definite noun is repeated while the meaning differs. Al-Baghawi related with his chain of narration from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what your Lord said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He says: Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed the blessing of monotheism anything but Paradise?" And that is the reward of the servant's good deed in its deed, in return for his Lord's good to him through nurturing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 61:

﴿So which of the blessings of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (p-187) That is, the great and beautiful blessings from the Noble Master, the Mighty, the Merciful, who combines all the attributes of perfection, ﴿will you deny?﴾ Is it the blessing of touch from above or other things, which Allah, glorified is He, made an example of the principle that whoever does good is rewarded with the like of his goodness? This verse is the conclusion of eight verses urging action that leads to the eight gates of the Garden of those brought near. And Allah is the Guide.

Since the opening of this discourse made known, from the mention of fear together with the attribute of honor, and from its close, which mentioned excellence (al-ihsan), that this group are those who do good, and since it is known that those who act are of various ranks, and that each rank's reward is in proportion to its deeds, the context required explaining what is prepared for those below them: ﴿And beneath them﴾, meaning: in a place of lower rank than the gardens of these people of excellence [the muqarrabun (those brought near)], ﴿two gardens﴾, meaning: for each one, for those below these people of excellence [among those who fear], and they are the companions of the right (aṣḥāb al-yamīn). Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "Beneath them in terms of their levels." Ibn Burjan made the four gardens distributed among all of them. He also said that the specification of this number indicates that they comprise what is in the four seasons of this world: winter, spring, summer and autumn. He interpreted by this the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Two gardens of gold, which I have been given, with what is in them, and two gardens of silver, which I have been given, with what is in them." Then he allowed that the intended meaning of "beneath" (al-dun) is the nearer to the human being, which is al-barzakh (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection). Thus these two would be for the people of the barzakh, just as ﴿And indeed for those who did wrong there is a punishment beneath that﴾ refers to the punishment of the grave.

﴿فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما﴾ That is: the Benefactor, who bestows His abundant blessings upon the highest and upon those beneath Him (p-188) ﴿تُكَذِّبانِ﴾ Is it the blessing of touch from below, or another of what God has made in this world as an example of this, such as that some gardens are superior to others, and other kinds of preference?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 64:

Since the water in these two gardens is less than the water in the other two, it might be thought that their water does not suffice for their full sufficiency, so He said: ﴿Dark green﴾, that is: green, a green that, from the intensity of irrigation, inclines to blackness, from al-duhma (darkness). Al-Asfahani (al-Isfahani) said: What predominates in these two gardens is plants and fragrant herbs spread over the face of the earth, while in the first two it is trees and fruits.

"So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?" That is: the blessings of the One who is good to the one above you and to whoever is below him, through the vastness of His mercy. "Will you deny?" Is it the blessing of the taste from the direction of the front, or other things which He made as an example of that from the gardens of the world, abundant in water and other things?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 66:

When the mention of that which indicates their irrigation had been made, he confirmed it with his saying: ﴿In them﴾, i.e., in every garden, for every person among them, ﴿are two springs gushing forth﴾, i.e., they bubble up with such force that they cause a spraying of water which does not cease. He did not mention their flowing, so it is as if they are such that they irrigate their garden without reaching the stage of flowing. Spraying (al-nadh) is less than flowing (al-jary) and more than sprinkling (al-nadh, with the unpointed letter, i.e., nadḥ). Al-Isfahani said: "The root of nadkh (al-nadkh) is with the dotted letter, and it ends here." It is as if they are for one whose eyes well up with tears so that they fill without flowing. Ibn Burjan said, in substance, that the reason for the non-flowing of the two springs is that they are modeled on the garden of autumn here and winter with it, because of the long time since water descended upon them and they settled in the depths of the earth, so that by the welling and gushing they rise upward, even though the Garden has no rain in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 67:

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ That is: which of the blessings of the Nurturer, who is most eloquent in wisdom in His nurturing, ﴿will you two deny?﴾ Is it the blessing of taste, from the direction of what lies behind the tongue, or other things of the kind, such as the gushing springs that boil up and do not flow, and the pipes made for gushing forth? For they are such that they delight the beholder by the rising of their jets with the force of their spring and their spraying, and they are among the great blessings.

When he had mentioned the irrigation and its cause, he mentioned what arises from it, saying: ﴿In both of them is fruit﴾, that is, of every kind of fruit. He singled out the most noble of them, and the most abundant in the autumn and winter, as in the gardens of this world which were made an example of these two gardens, saying: ﴿and palm trees and pomegranates﴾. For each of them is both fruit and condiment. So he singled them out for honour and to draw attention to the enjoyment of fruit that is in them. The first of them (the palm) is more widely beneficial and more wondrous in its creation, which is why it was placed first.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ That is: the blessings of the One who did good to you both, O you two weighty ones (al-thaqalan, jinn and humankind), through His magnificent nurture. ﴿Will you deny?﴾ Is it the blessing of the tasting from the right, or from other than it, of what has been made an example of this from the gardens of the world, and other than that?

When what he mentioned (the pleasure of the Garden) cannot be complete without companions, and it has been reported that in some of the fruits of Paradise and in the fruit-bearing of its trees there are women and youths, just as the like of these is found within the waters of this world, [Allah said], "And We made from water every living thing" (Al-Anbiya' 21:30), he said, gathering in the manner of the indication already passed, that the two Gardens are for each individual of this category: "therein" (فِيهِنَّ), i.e., in the four Gardens, or in the Gardens that are specified for the women. Ibn Burjan allowed that the pronoun may refer to the fruits, the palm trees and the pomegranates, for women and youths come into being from them (p-190) within the inner skin of the pomegranate and the like. "Good (khayrat)," i.e., women in whom there is abundant goodness. Its original form is khayyir, with the doubled letter, because khayr, when used as a comparative, is not made into the sound plural. Perhaps it was lightened because they are characterized by lightness in their existence and in all their affairs, and because these two Gardens are below those before them. "Beautiful (hisan)," i.e., in the utmost beauty, in form and in character.

"So which of the favors of your Lord, both of you, will you deny?" That is: which of the bounties of the One who is perfect in beneficence toward you both? ﴿Will you deny﴾: is it the blessing of the taste (of the fruits) from the direction of the left, or from other than it, from the One who made it an example for the creation of women, children, garments and adornments from the fruits of the trees and the crops, which come from the waters by which life is sustained? In these there is generation and other things that reflection brings forth for the people of insight, because everything in Paradise arises from the word, from the provision, just as it arises from Him, glorified is He, in this abode through causation... and wisdom.

Then He clarified them with His saying: ﴿Ḥūrun﴾ (ḥūr), meaning they have eyes of intense blackness of black and intense whiteness of white. Ibn Jarir said: "bīḍ" is the plural (of abyad, white). ﴿Maqṣūrāt﴾ (restrained), meaning: confined to their husbands and kept within, guarding them against being made common. It is a metaphor (kināya) for their greatness. ﴿Fi l-khiyām﴾ (in pavilions), which are of hollow, translucent pearl, as a reward for the one who restrained his self from ... Allah, so he withheld his limbs from slips and guarded his heart from heedlessness.

Then which of the bounties of your Lord would you two deny? [That is], which of the favors of the One of Majesty and Bounty toward you two? ﴿Would you deny﴾: the blessing of the taste that comes from above (p. 191), or other than it, of what He made an example of this in the world? For just as He created us from dust and then shaped us through the stages of creation according to the wisdom of causes, so He created those [gardens] from the earth of Paradise, its meadows and its fruits, by the word of "be" (kun), without causes.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 74:

Since the souls of the righteous, those of lofty and great aspirations, are inclined toward the virgins, He said: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ — that is, no one has exercised any kind of dominion over them. He generalized the time by omitting the preposition, so He said: ﴿before them﴾ — that is, the aforementioned touching has been negated throughout all the time that preceded the touching of the people of these gardens of them. Had it occurred at any moment of the moments of that prior time, the negation would not be true. ﴿Nor jinn﴾. Thus they are in the utmost of exclusivity, each one with what is with him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 75:

﴿Then which﴾ [al-Rahman: 77], meaning: as a consequence of this multiplicity, for such great blessings, We say, in wonder at the one who denies, as a rebuke to him and as a reminder of the blessings of Allah Most High, which cannot be counted: "Which of the ﴿bounties of your Lord﴾, that is, the magnificent blessings from the One who manages your affairs with His complete power and His overwhelming, all-encompassing greatness, ﴿do you two deny﴾? Is it the blessing of the silk lining beneath [the garments], or some other of the things He has made as an example of this, such as the virgin maidens who are kept secluded, and all the general and apparent blessings mentioned, in every state, in this world and the Hereafter?" It was concluded with the affirmation that there are twenty-four [blessings]: eight of them at the beginning of the surah are worldly blessings, and sixteen are gardens. He arranged them in this number to indicate their greatness by multiplying them, for it is a complete number, since it comprises the greatest number of fractions. For this reason the dirham and other things were divided into twenty-four qirats (a unit of weight, one twenty-fourth of a dirham or dinar).

When the demonstration through the blessings that encompass the six directions and the five senses had been completed in the most perfect manner, by warding off harms and bringing benefits, as was already indicated by the words ﴿So is there any who will take heed?﴾ in al-Qamar, with its goodness toward the five senses, and by its repetition, and by the repetition of ﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ six times, corresponding to the six directions, from front and back, He concluded them with one further blessing. This indicates that the cause of all this is belief in the Oneness of the One, Exalted is He, a belief which obliges submission to the command of the messenger whenever it comes from Him, Exalted is He. Therefore it is a blessing that never ceases at all. Rather, whenever one cycle of it is completed, another new cycle begins, and so on without any end, just as the One, which is the root of all numbers, has no end at all. This blessing, which indicates lasting rest, is the one intended in itself, in a manner that is no more wondrous nor more noble than it. Thus He, Exalted is He, said, explaining the state of the people of goodness and those below them, who share in that rest, in what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived: ﴿Reclining﴾, meaning that they have this in the state of reclining as a constant habit, because they have no occupation whatsoever except enjoyment. ﴿On rafraf﴾, meaning garments of soft fabric and cushions of finely woven brocade, soft, with great pillows, [and] dazzling gardens, and carpets with noble edges. The rafraf of the clouds is their fringe, meaning their hanging skirt.

Since green is the most beautiful and most delightful of colours, He said: ﴿Green cushions and beautiful carpets﴾, meaning: complete furnishings of carpets and other things, which in their perfection and strangeness seem as though they were made by the jinn, because of their attribution to their land. In the al-Qamus it is said: ʿAbqar is a place abounding in jinn, and a village whose construction is of the utmost beauty. The ʿabqari (ʿabqariyy) is the perfect one of anything, and the chief, and the one above whom there is nothing. Al-Razi said: it means embroidered cushions (ṭanāfis mukhammala). Ibn Jarir said: ṭanāfis thick ones. Al-Qushayri said: among the Arabs, the ʿabqari is every patterned garment. Al-Khalil said: every noble, precious, splendid thing, whether of men or others. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) about ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "I have not seen an ʿabqari among people who speaks as he does." Qutrub said: it is not from the nisba forms; rather, it is in the same position as kursiyy and bukhtiyy.

Since what is meant by it is the genus, He indicated its abundance by the plural, while using the singular form, to point to the unity of its perfection in beauty, and so He said: ﴿Beautiful﴾, meaning they are in the utmost perfection of craftsmanship and beauty of appearance, which cannot be described.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 55, verse 77:

﴿Then which of the bounties of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ That is, the great blessings from the One Benefactor, besides whom there is no benefactor, and no beneficence except from Him. His blessings cannot be counted, and His praise cannot be enumerated. ﴿Deny?﴾ With this verse the eight blessings specific to the Garden of the People of the Right (Jannat Ashab al-Yamin) are complete, indicating the deed that leads to its eight gates. And God is the Granter of success.

When what was mentioned in this surah of blessings pointed to the all-encompassing perfection of its Originator, and when the last blessing indicated by allusion that His blessings have no end, since He, although possessing all perfection, is exalted above any trace of deficiency, the fitting conclusion to the blessings of the Hereafter was His saying, corresponding to the conclusion of the blessings of this world, where He expressed by "permanence" (al-baqa') what He had mentioned before it, namely "annihilation" (al-fana'). This carries blessing (al-barakah) as an allusion (p-194) to the fact that His blessings have no cessation: ﴿Blessed﴾. Ibn Burjan said: it is from tafa'ala (the form indicating intensity) of blessing (al-barakah), and He, may His remembrance be exalted, is not mentioned with it except in a matter that is wondrous. Its meaning is that He is established in a stability that the minds cannot encompass in describing Him. It is in the form of mufa'alah, which indicates exerting effort, when the one addressed is one whose opposition can be contested. This comes together with abundance, blessing and beneficence.

Since the magnification of the Name is more firmly rooted and more eloquent in magnifying the one named, He said: ﴿The name of your Lord﴾, that is, the One who bestows favour upon you by sending down this Qur'an, which has disposed you to follow it, so that you became a manifestation of it and it became a disposition for you. Thus His beneficence towards you exceeds description. For this reason He described the Lord, in the reading of the majority, as: ﴿Possessor of Majesty﴾, that is, of overwhelming greatness, so He is the One who takes vengeance upon the enemies; ﴿and Honour﴾, that is, of beneficence that cannot be fully encompassed, so He is the One characterized by the most holy beauty, which necessitates the overflowing of mercy upon all the friends of God. The reading of Ibn 'Amir is "Dhu" (Possessor) as an attribute of the Name, and likewise it is in the codices of the people of Syria. The last two attributes are of the kind of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one element is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, and vice versa): in the first he omitted from the first the object of the attribute, which is vengeance upon the enemies, and from the second the effect of honour, which is mercy upon the friends. Thus affirming the attribute first indicates the omission of its opposite second, and affirming the verb second indicates the omission of its opposite first.

Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': it seems that he means by the Name with which the surah began, and the end of the surah has been linked to its beginning in a more general manner, so that it includes honour through the teaching of the Qur'an and other things, and vengeance through the admission into the fires and other things. And God, glory be to Him and exalted, is the One who grants success to what is correct.
